display.purpose: The home masthead and nothing else. Fraunces 720, oldstyle numerals (text-display).

headline.purpose: One per page; the default h1 (text-page-title).

title.purpose: Section headings and the impact ledger's figures; the default h2 (text-section-title).

card-title.purpose: A product's name under its plate, a row title, a dialog title (text-card-title). A subsection step exists at 1.075rem / 560 (text-subsection).

body.purpose: Reading text. Lead paragraphs use 1.125rem with text-pretty; descriptions 0.875-1rem in Ink Muted.

label.purpose: The wall label (label-mono): kickers, certifications, values, dates, counts, order numbers, the catalogue line under a plate. Uppercase, tracked, tabular numerals, Ink Muted.

figure.purpose: A price, quantity, total or impact number on a ledger row: mono, tabular-nums, 0.875rem. Never in a filled band.

shadows.name: header-sheet
shadows.purpose: The sticky header only, so it reads as a separate sheet when content scrolls under it. One of the two sanctioned shadows (The Two Sheets Rule); allowlisted by file in scripts/check-design-system.mjs.

shadows.name: cta-ledge
shadows.purpose: The primary button (cta-primary) only: a 1px ledge beneath its border so the one filled button feels pressed onto the page. Removed when disabled. No other content surface carries a shadow at rest or on hover.

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Button, field and link colour/border transitions (--duration-fast).

motion.name: duration-default
motion.purpose: Tailwind default transition duration; plate border warming (--duration-default).

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Every hover and focus transition on the notebook utilities.

motion.name: cta-press
motion.purpose: Primary and secondary buttons press one pixel down.

motion.name: ink-underline
motion.value: transform 240ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); scaleX(0) to scaleX(1) from the left
motion.purpose: A link's underline scored in under the cursor or focus ring. The site's only authored motion; none under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: loading
motion.purpose: The only things that move while nothing else is happening. No shimmer sweep.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: animation-duration and transition-duration 0.01ms; loaders (animate-pulse, animate-spin, .loading-spinner) slow to 3s instead of stopping
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion policy. 0.01ms rather than 0s so transitionend still fires.

components.name: Primary Button

narrative.overview:
Link Flame is a shopkeeper's notebook. Every product is an entry: a square photo plate like a print pasted onto the page, a name in serif, and one catalogue line in mono underneath — BLUELAND · B CORP · 120 BOTTLES/YR — brand, certification, impact figure. The numbers are the product. The site's claim is "Measured, not promised", so figures are set in mono, tabular, on hairline-ruled ledger rows, and never in a filled band.

The notebook is the same stationery as lscaturchio.xyz and InfiniStar, by design: warm off-white paper with a near-invisible grain, structure drawn with hairlines and space rather than boxes, a serif with personality for what the shop says, a plain sans for what the shopper reads, and a monospace label beside every piece of metadata. What tells the three notebooks apart is the pen. The personal site writes in forest green, InfiniStar in mulberry; Link Flame writes in Moss — a green that is dirt and leaf rather than mint and marketing, dark enough to be the only colour on the page and still read as the brand.

What Link Flame keeps that the siblings do not have: the product plate as the recurring unit of the catalogue, the impact ledger of summed figures, and a storefront — cart, checkout, orders, subscriptions, loyalty — which the notebook language extends to as rows on paper.

The system deliberately is not three things. It is not the screened-shelf storefront it replaced: no honey-amber accent, no brown-tinted shadows, no gradient washes behind sections, no sweep-of-light button, no card that lifts on hover. It is not SaaS furniture: no three-column feature tiles, no pill badges as decoration, no count-up numerals. And it is not a theme engine: one kind of paper, read by day or by night.
keyCharacteristics: One paper ground, warm off-white with a fixed 3.5% noise grain; dark mode is a night variant of the same page.
One ink, Moss, spent sparingly: links, hover, selection, the focus outline, the mark, the single primary button per view.
Hairline rules and tint shifts structure the page; there are no floating cards and no decorative shadows.
Three type voices with fixed jobs: Fraunces speaks, Instrument Sans reads, IBM Plex Mono catalogues.
Squareness marks the work (product plates); roundness marks the interface (controls, chips, pills).
Figures are mono and tabular on hairline rows — the ledger, not the banner.
Motion is the interface responding to the shopper, never the page introducing itself.

rules.name: The One Pen Rule
rules.body: Moss is the only chromatic accent on any surface, and it marks action or emphasis, never area. If a screen has moss in more than a few places, it has too many. No gradient anywhere, on anything.

rules.name: The Sand Hairline Rule
rules.body: Dividers are 1px of Hairline, sand-toned, never neutral grey and never thicker. Depth of structure is expressed by more rules and more space, not by darker lines.

rules.name: The Tinted Paper Rule
rules.body: A "contained" surface is the same paper at a different tint (Paper Card lighter, Paper Tinted darker), bordered by a hairline. It is never a white box on a grey page.

rules.name: The Wall Label Rule
rules.body: Every piece of metadata (a date, a count, a brand, a certification) is set as a Label: mono, small, uppercase, tracked, muted. Metadata never borrows the body or heading voice. Every section, row and figure introduces itself with one before its title — the kicker is the house device.

rules.name: The Serif Speaks Rule
rules.body: Fraunces appears only where the shop is speaking: h1–h6, the type-scale utilities, the wordmark, product names, the impact ledger's figures. Never in body copy, UI controls, prices or labels. font-display on a non-heading fails the build unless the element carries data-voice="display"; font-serif is a transitional alias the ratchet is counting down.

rules.name: The Measured Figure Rule
rules.body: Any number that counts — a price, a total, an impact figure, a stock level — is set in mono with tabular-nums, on paper, on a hairline row. Figures are never set in a filled band, never count up on entry, and never borrow a status colour to look impressive.

rules.name: The Flat Paper Rule
rules.body: No shadow on any content surface, at rest or on hover. A hovered surface changes tint and border colour; it does not rise. The brown shadow-warm-* vocabulary is gone from the theme.

rules.name: The Two Sheets Rule
rules.body: The only elevated objects are the sticky header and the primary button's 1px ledge. Nothing else may add a shadow without changing DESIGN.md first.

rules.name: The Scrim Rule
rules.body: A modal separates with a scrim, not a shadow. overlay-scrim — hsl(var(--scrim) / var(--scrim-alpha)), ink in both themes, 25% on paper and 55% at night — is the third sanctioned separation mechanism, and the only one available to an overlay, since the Two Sheets Rule has already spent both of its shadows.

rules.name: The Square Plate Rule
rules.body: A product's photograph is a square 1:1 plate with 0px corners and a 1px hairline, object-cover, no hover scale, no gradient scrim over the image — the print, pasted onto the ledger. Squareness marks the work; roundness marks the interface.

dos: Do introduce every section, row and figure with a wall label before its title.
Do divide with 1px sand hairlines and 64–96px of vertical space; let whitespace and rules do the structuring.
Do spend Moss on action and emphasis only: links, hover, selection, the mark, one primary button per view.
Do build text-led lists as hairline-divided rows and keep products as square plates in a gallery grid.
Do route every colour through the tokens; status is text-success, text-warning, text-info, text-destructive and their -muted washes.
Do set every price, quantity, total and impact figure in mono with tabular-nums, on paper.
Do design dark mode as the same notebook at night: cool hue-220 page, the ink lifted to 100 30% 70%, hairlines at 18% lightness.
Do give an empty section an honest empty state in the same voice: a wall label, one serif line, one primary action.
Do keep the one primary button per view; the second action is outline or link.
donts: Don't add shadows to content surfaces at rest or on hover; the header sheet and the CTA ledge are the only elevated objects.
Don't reintroduce gradients, glow, glass cards or the brown shadow vocabulary; the screened shelf is gone.
Don't build SaaS furniture: three-column feature tiles, pill badges as decoration, count-up numerals.
Don't use monospace as a voice. It is the label beside the work and the figure on the row, never headings or body copy; the site is not a terminal.
Don't set Fraunces in body text, controls, prices or labels, and don't set body copy in anything but Instrument Sans.
Don't use neutral grey for rules or muted surfaces; every neutral is warm paper (hue 30–38) in light mode and cool night (hue 220) in dark.
Don't introduce a second accent colour; Moss Soft exists for secondary fills and the four signal colours are for status only. Honey is gone.
Don't round a product plate, scale it on hover or lay a badge over it; squareness marks the work.
